content: Asia's richest man Mukesh ‌Ambani's telecoms and digital unit Jio Platforms is set to list in Mumbai on Wednesday, after its $3.2 billion IPO drew $77 billion in bids in ​India's most-subscribed offering ever. headline_en: Search launched for four missing fishermen off Kudawella Coast
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Search launched for four missing fishermen off Kudawella Coast
summary_en: Search launched for four missing fishermen off Kudawella Coast
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Search launched for four missing fishermen off Kudawella Coast
content: The Sri Lanka Navy and Air Force have launched search operations to locate a fishing boat carrying four fishermen that went missing after departing from the Kudawella area in Matara. According to the Navy, the vessel left for fishing activities on October 21. The fishermen last communicated with the boat’s owner on October 23. However, contact with the vessel was subsequently lost, prompting its owner to lodge a complaint with the authorities. Following the complaint, the Navy launched search operations with the assistance of the Sri Lanka Air Force to locate the missing vessel and its crew. Meanwhile, search operations are also continuing to locate another fishing boat carrying three fishermen that went missing after departing for fishing activities from the Pudumathalan area in Mullaitivu. The Navy stated that efforts to locate the second vessel and its crew are still underway.

headline_en: Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery with missile
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery with missile
summary_en: Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery with missile
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura oil refinery with missile
content: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Tuesday they had hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the biggest in the kingdom, with a ballistic missile. Intensifying hostilities between Yemen and Saudi Arabia have further disrupted oil supplies and heightened the risk of a wider regional conflict, eight months since the Iran war began. The Houthis also said they had attacked Saudi military aircraft and repelled an advance by Saudi-backed forces near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an important Red Sea shipping route. The Houthis' military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said the strike on the Ras Tanura refinery had caused a fire at the complex, ⁠which also includes a shipping terminal and is located on the Gulf, west of the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the strike. Ras Tanura, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, was shut for a period in the early months of the Iran war as a precautionary measure. Nearly all Saudi Arabia's oil exports flow through two main ports: Ras Tanura in the Gulf and Yanbu on the Red Sea, both of which the Houthis have attacked in the past. Bloomberg News cited a person familiar with the matter as saying Saudi Arabia had contained a fire near Ras Tanura's terminal. The Houthis said they had attacked two military transport jets at Najran Airport and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. They also said they attacked the Saudi defence ministry building in Riyadh, and Abha airport. There was no ⁠immediate Saudi confirmation of the attacks. On Tuesday afternoon, civil defence authorities briefly issued an air raid alert in the Saudi capital Riyadh. Falling debris from the interception of two ballistic missiles over Riyadh caused material damage to a building, a construction site and a vehicle, the Saudi Civil Defence said later on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government said it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by ⁠the Houthis towards Riyadh. The Houthis said they had repelled an advance by forces they described as Saudi-backed from the southern approaches to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces earlier this month pushed the Houthis out of coastal areas they had seized in September, loosening the group's grip on a vital Red ⁠Sea oil route. Houthi-affiliated Al Masirah TV reported Saudi strikes on the Yemeni city of Mocha. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. The fighting has shattered a 2022 UN-brokered truce between the coalition and the Houthis, who control the Yemeni capital Sanaa. On Monday, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and ⁠Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran to try to reduce regional tensions. Parliament in Egypt, which has said it is considering joining the three countries in a mutual defence pact, authorised Egypt's military on Monday to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked.

headline_en: Tourist arrivals in October top 135,000
headline_si: ශ්‍රී ලංකා පුවත්: Tourist arrivals in October top 135,000
summary_en: Tourist arrivals in October top 135,000
summary_si: මෙම පුවත Daily FT වෙබ් අඩවියෙන් ලබා ගන්නා ලදී. Tourist arrivals in October top 135,000
content: The number of tourists that have arrived in Sri Lanka so far this month has surpassed 135,000. Sri Lanka welcomed 136,096 international tourists in the first 25 days of October, with India continuing to dominate the tourism market, according to the latest figures released by the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA). India accounted for 51,424 arrivals, representing around 38% of all tourists who visited Sri Lanka during the month. The United Kingdom was the second-largest source market, recording 10,117 arrivals, while China ranked third with 9,411 visitors. Australia and Germany rounded out the top five markets, with 6,844 and 6,269 arrivals respectively. The October figures pushed Sri Lanka’s cumulative tourist arrivals for 2026 to 1,829,772. India remained the largest contributor during the January-October period with 488,838 arrivals, followed by the United Kingdom with 170,844. China recorded 121,961 arrivals, while Germany contributed 103,547 and Australia 93,833.
